# k0rdent_regions (Data Source)

Every region the token can reach.

Region ids are operator-declared and there is no published list, so without this the only way to fill in the provider's `region` is to be told one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The regions you can use.
data "k0rdent_regions" "all" {}

output "region_ids" {
  value = data.k0rdent_regions.all.ids
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `include_global` (Boolean) Include the `global` control-plane tier even where it holds no compute. Left out, `global` is listed only where it hosts projects, which is the all-in-one install that runs compute under it.

### Read-Only

- `ids` (List of String) Just the ids, for `for_each` and `contains`. Sorted by `id` alongside `regions`, so `ids[i]` is the id of `regions[i]`.
- `project_region_ids` (List of String) The ids of the regions that host projects, sorted: the values a `k0rdent_project`'s `region` takes. The contract asks a client offering a choice of project region to offer these, not the `regional` ones.
- `regions` (Attributes List) The regions. Sorted by `id`.

That order holds when the platform returns the same regions in a different order, but not when a region is added: one sorting ahead of the rest shifts every index after it. Prefer `for_each` over `[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--regions))

<a id="nestedatt--regions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `regions`

Read-Only:

- `hosts_projects` (Boolean) Whether a project can be created here: the regions a `k0rdent_project`'s `region` accepts. Every `regional` region does. `global` does only on an installation that runs compute under it.
- `id` (String) The value that goes in the provider's `region`.
- `type` (String) `regional` or `global`.

## Related

- [`k0rdent_cluster_types`](../data-sources/cluster_types.md) data source: lists what a region offers to build clusters from.
- [`k0rdent_address_pools`](../data-sources/address_pools.md) data source: lists the pools a region allocates subnets from.
